title: Quantum key distribution over free space optic (FSO) channel using higher order Gaussian beam spatial modes
authors: Kamran, M; Khan, MM; Malik, T; Arfeen, A
Main Research Question: How can the KMB09 protocol be practically implemented in a QKD system using higher dimensional photon states to enhance secure communication over long distances?
Methods and Experiments: The study proposes a practical implementation framework for the KMB09 protocol, utilizing higher dimensional photon states encoded in higher order Gaussian beam spatial modes. The simulation setup includes a laser source, attenuators, beam expanders, spatial light modulators (SLM), and single-photon detectors. The simulation tests the protocol's efficiency in two and four dimensions of photon states, using computer-generated binary holograms to control the spatial modes of the laser beams.
Results: The simulation results demonstrate that the system's efficiency converges to expected theoretical values, with an efficiency of 0.25 for two-dimensional states and 0.3683 for four-dimensional states. These results align with the numerical and analytical predictions for the KMB09 protocol, confirming the feasibility of the proposed implementation framework.
Discussion: The study discusses the challenges and innovative approaches in the practical implementation of the KMB09 protocol. It highlights the use of higher dimensional photon states and the role of spatial light modulators in managing the complex beam spatial modes required for the protocol. The comparison with theoretical predictions validates the effectiveness of the simulation setup and the potential of the KMB09 protocol for enhancing the security and distance of QKD systems.
Conclusions: The proposed framework successfully demonstrates the practical implementation of the KMB09 protocol using higher order Gaussian beam spatial modes. The simulation results are consistent with theoretical expectations, proving the protocol's potential to enhance secure quantum key distribution over long distances. Future work will focus on further optimization and testing under various environmental conditions.
Future Work: Future research will explore the integration of additional quantum states and dimensions, the impact of atmospheric turbulence on the protocol's efficiency, and the development of robust error correction techniques to further enhance the security and reliability of the KMB09 protocol in practical QKD systems.
Proposed Keywords: ['Quantum Key Distribution', 'KMB09 Protocol', 'Higher Dimensional Photon States', 'Gaussian Beam Spatial Modes', 'Practical Implementation of QKD']

title: Secrecy enhancement of RF backhaul system with parallel FSO communication link
authors: Ai, Y; Mathur, A; Lei, HJ; Cheffena, M; Ansari, IS
Main Research Question: How can the physical layer secrecy (PLS) performance of a hybrid FSO/RF communication system be enhanced under various atmospheric and hardware impairments?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs a modified selection combining scheme for a hybrid FSO/RF system, considering both secrecy performance and diversity gain. The analysis includes the effects of atmospheric turbulence, FSO receiver pointing errors, and RF power amplifier inefficiencies. Exact analytical expressions for performance indicators such as average secrecy capacity (ASC) and secrecy outage probability (SOP) are derived. Asymptotic SOP analysis is also conducted to provide deeper insights into system performance under extreme conditions.
Results: The results demonstrate that the hybrid FSO/RF system, under the modified selection combining scheme, effectively enhances the physical layer secrecy performance. The system shows improved resilience to atmospheric conditions and hardware inefficiencies. The derived analytical expressions accurately predict the system's performance, which is validated through simulations comparing various system setups.
Discussion: The study highlights the effectiveness of integrating FSO and RF systems to enhance secrecy performance in communication systems. The inclusion of atmospheric turbulence and pointing errors in the FSO link, along with power amplifier inefficiencies in the RF link, provides a realistic assessment of the system's performance. The results suggest that the modified selection combining scheme offers significant benefits in terms of secrecy enhancement and system robustness against eavesdropping.
Conclusions: The hybrid FSO/RF system with a modified selection combining scheme significantly enhances the physical layer secrecy performance. The system is robust against various atmospheric and hardware impairments, making it a viable solution for secure communication in next-generation networks. Future work should focus on optimizing system parameters and exploring the integration of advanced cryptographic techniques to further enhance security.
Future Work: Future research directions include optimizing the system parameters for enhanced performance, integrating advanced cryptographic techniques with the hybrid FSO/RF system, and exploring the impact of more complex atmospheric conditions and hardware impairments on system performance.
Proposed Keywords: ['Hybrid FSO/RF System', 'Physical Layer Secrecy', 'Atmospheric Turbulence', 'Power Amplifier Inefficiency', 'Secrecy Outage Probability']

title: Analysis of selection combining hybrid FSO/RF systems considering physical layer security and interference
authors: Liang, HD; Li, YM; Miao, MK; Gao, C; Li, XF
Main Research Question: How does the hybrid FSO/RF communication system perform under the influence of non-cooperative targets (NCT) including eavesdroppers and jammers, and what are the implications of using selection combining technique at the receiver?
Methods and Experiments: The study models the FSO link using Málaga( ) distribution and the RF link using Nakagami-m distribution, considering pointing errors. A selection combining technique is used at the receiver, which selects the highest SNR from both links without requiring channel state information from the transmitter. The study derives closed-form expressions for outage probability, average bit error rate, and secrecy outage probability, and conducts simulations to validate these metrics.
Results: The results indicate that the hybrid FSO/RF system outperforms traditional FSO systems in terms of outage probability, average bit error rate, and secrecy outage probability, even in the presence of RF interference. The study also provides asymptotic performance analysis, demonstrating the robustness of the hybrid system against interference and eavesdropping.
Discussion: The paper discusses the effectiveness of the hybrid FSO/RF system in mitigating the effects of eavesdropping and jamming by leveraging the complementary characteristics of FSO and RF links. The use of selection combining at the receiver is highlighted as a significant factor in enhancing system performance without the need for transmitter channel state information.
Conclusions: The study concludes that the hybrid FSO/RF system, modeled with Málaga and Nakagami-m distributions and employing selection combining, offers superior performance compared to standalone FSO systems. This system is particularly effective in environments with non-cooperative targets such as eavesdroppers and jammers.
Future Work: Future research should explore the integration of more advanced modulation techniques and consider the impact of more complex interference scenarios. Additionally, extending the analysis to different types of fading models and exploring the potential of machine learning techniques for adaptive selection combining could further enhance the performance and reliability of hybrid FSO/RF systems.
Proposed Keywords: ['Hybrid FSO/RF System', 'Physical Layer Security', 'Non-Cooperative Target', 'Selection Combining Technique', 'Málaga Distribution']

title: Secure and covert communication strategy of UAV based on hybrid RF/FSO system
authors: Song, XK; Wang, X; Zhao, SH; Li, YJ; Li, X; Zhang, XW
Main Research Question: How can the communication security of UAVs be enhanced using a hybrid RF/FSO system to address both secure and covert communication challenges?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs a hybrid RF/FSO communication system for UAVs, focusing on secure and covert communication strategies. For secure communication, the system transmits data concurrently through RF and FSO links, considering active eavesdropping scenarios. For covert communication, the RF link is used to generate interfering signals to aid the FSO link in covert operations. The research derives closed-form expressions for SOP and EST, and formulates an optimization problem to maximize EST considering constraints like transmit power and detection error probability. A two-stage gradient-based iterative solution algorithm is developed for this optimization.
Results: The results include derived expressions for SOP and EST, demonstrating the effectiveness of the hybrid RF/FSO system in enhancing UAV communication security. The optimization problem for maximizing EST under covert communication constraints is effectively solved using the proposed algorithm, showing significant improvements in communication security metrics.
Discussion: The study discusses the advantages of integrating RF and FSO technologies in UAV communications to enhance security against eavesdropping and interference. It highlights the importance of considering both secure and covert communication strategies in UAV systems, especially in environments with high RF challenges. The effectiveness of the proposed two-stage solution algorithm is also validated through numerical results.
Conclusions: The hybrid RF/FSO system significantly enhances the security and covertness of UAV communications. The study confirms that employing concurrent transmission through RF and FSO links, along with strategic interference generation, effectively mitigates risks associated with eavesdropping and interference. The proposed optimization framework and solution algorithm provide a robust approach for maximizing EST while ensuring covert communication.
Future Work: Future research should explore adaptive strategies for dynamic adjustment of transmission power and interference generation based on real-time channel and threat assessments. Additionally, integrating machine learning techniques could further optimize the security and efficiency of hybrid RF/FSO systems in UAV communications.
Proposed Keywords: ['Hybrid RF/FSO System', 'UAV Communication Security', 'Secrecy Outage Probability', 'Effective Secrecy Throughput', 'Covert Communication']

title: The probability of error in FSO communication system using Differential Chaos Shift Keying
authors: Narang, G; Aggarwal, M; Kaushal, H; Ahuja, S
Main Research Question: How does the Differential Chaos Shift Keying (DCSK) technique affect the performance of Free-Space Optical (FSO) communication systems under various turbulence conditions, link lengths, and spreading factors?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs the DCSK modulation technique in an FSO communication system under the Gamma-Gamma turbulence model. The performance metrics analyzed include the probability of error across different link lengths, spreading factors, and turbulence intensities. The system model incorporates chaotic signals to enhance security, with the chaotic nature of the signals providing inherent security against interception by unintended receivers.
Results: The results indicate that increasing the spreading factor improves the average signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) but also increases the probability of error under the same link length and turbulence conditions. This trade-off suggests a compromise must be made between achieving high SNR and maintaining system security in DCSK-based FSO systems.
Discussion: The study highlights the challenges in balancing security and performance in FSO communication systems using DCSK. While DCSK enhances security due to the chaotic nature of the signals, it also necessitates higher SNR to maintain low error rates, particularly under strong turbulence conditions. The findings underscore the complexity of designing FSO systems that are both secure and efficient.
Conclusions: The research concludes that DCSK is a viable modulation technique for enhancing the security of FSO communications. However, the increased security comes at the cost of higher SNR requirements, especially as the spreading factor increases. Future FSO systems using DCSK must carefully balance these aspects to optimize both security and performance.
Future Work: Future research should explore the integration of advanced error-correction techniques to mitigate the increased error rates associated with higher spreading factors in DCSK-based FSO systems. Additionally, studies could investigate the impact of varying atmospheric conditions more comprehensively to refine the Gamma-Gamma model parameters for better prediction of system performance.
Proposed Keywords: ['Free-Space Optical Communications', 'Differential Chaos Shift Keying', 'Gamma-Gamma Turbulence', 'Signal-to-Noise Ratio', 'Communication Security']

title: On mitigating reactive jamming with dynamic resource allocation in optical IRS and UAV-assisted FSO-based networks
authors: Singh, P; Salameh, HB; Bohara, VA; Srivastava, A; Ayyash, M
Main Research Question: How can reactive jamming attacks be mitigated in UAV-assisted FSO-based networks while satisfying users' QoS requirements?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs a binary linear programming approach to allocate mirror elements in UAV-assisted FSO networks, considering reactive jamming. A batch-based sequential fixing linear programming procedure, Reactive Jamming-Aware Mirror Element Allocation (RJA-MEA), is introduced to optimize mirror element assignment. Simulations compare the RJA-MEA scheme against Reactive Jamming Unaware-Mirror Element Allocation (RJU-MEA), Reactive Jamming-Aware Equal Mirror Element Allocation (RJA-EMEA), and Reactive Jamming Unaware-Equal Mirror Element Allocation (RJU-EMEA) under various jamming conditions.
Results: The RJA-MEA scheme demonstrated superior performance in mitigating reactive jamming effects compared to RJU-MEA, RJA-EMEA, and RJU-EMEA schemes. It significantly improved the network's sum rate performance by optimally allocating mirror elements based on the reactive jamming-aware strategy.
Discussion: The study highlights the effectiveness of the RJA-MEA scheme in enhancing network reliability and performance under reactive jamming scenarios. It addresses the limitations of previous schemes by incorporating a jamming-aware resource allocation strategy, which is crucial for security-sensitive applications in next-generation networks.
Conclusions: The RJA-MEA scheme effectively mitigates reactive jamming in UAV-assisted FSO networks, significantly enhancing network performance by optimally allocating mirror elements. This approach provides a resilient communication infrastructure for security-sensitive applications, suggesting its potential applicability in enhancing the robustness of next-generation networks against reactive jamming attacks.
Future Work: Future research should explore the extension of the RJA-MEA scheme to multi-UAV scenarios and optimize the 3D positioning of UAVs within specified areas to further enhance network performance and reliability under diverse operational conditions.
Proposed Keywords: ['Free-Space Optical Communications', 'Reactive Jamming Mitigation', 'UAV-Assisted Networks', 'Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces', 'Optimization in Communication Networks']

title: On the secrecy capacity of hybrid FSO-mmWave links with correlated wiretap channels
authors: Tokgoz, SC; Althunibat, S; Miller, SL; Qaraqe, KA
Main Research Question: How can the secrecy capacity of hybrid FSO-mmWave communication systems be analyzed and enhanced in the presence of correlated wiretap channels and different types of eavesdroppers?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs a theoretical analysis combined with Monte-Carlo simulations to evaluate the secrecy performance of hybrid FSO-mmWave systems. The analysis considers gamma-gamma turbulence models for FSO links and Nakagami-m fading for mmWave links. Different scenarios involving various types of eavesdroppers (RF-only, FSO-only, and hybrid) and their proximity to the legitimate transmitter or receiver (Eve-near-Alice and Eve-near-Bob) are examined. Analytical expressions for the probability of strictly positive secrecy capacity (SPSC) are derived, considering the correlation between the main and eavesdropper channels.
Results: The results demonstrate that the secrecy performance of hybrid FSO-mmWave systems is significantly influenced by the type of eavesdropper and their proximity to the communication links. The study finds that hybrid eavesdroppers (those capable of intercepting both FSO and mmWave signals) pose the greatest threat to secrecy. Additionally, the proximity of the eavesdropper to the legitimate transmitter (Eve-near-Alice scenario) generally results in a higher risk of secrecy breach compared to their proximity to the receiver (Eve-near-Bob).
Discussion: The findings highlight the critical impact of eavesdropper capabilities and positions on the security of hybrid FSO-mmWave systems. The study emphasizes the need for robust security measures that consider both types of links and potential eavesdropping scenarios. Comparisons with existing works suggest that the incorporation of physical-layer security techniques, tailored to the specific characteristics of hybrid systems, is essential for enhancing security.
Conclusions: The study concludes that hybrid FSO-mmWave systems, while promising for high data rate transmissions, require careful consideration of security aspects, particularly the type of eavesdropper and their position relative to the communication setup. The derived analytical expressions for SPSC provide valuable insights for designing more secure systems. Future work should focus on developing adaptive security mechanisms that dynamically respond to the changing environment and threat levels.
Future Work: Future research directions include exploring adaptive security mechanisms that can dynamically adjust based on real-time assessments of eavesdropper capabilities and channel conditions. Additionally, investigating the integration of advanced cryptographic techniques with physical-layer security measures could further enhance the robustness of hybrid FSO-mmWave systems against sophisticated attacks.
Proposed Keywords: ['Hybrid FSO-mmWave Systems', 'Physical-Layer Security', 'Secrecy Capacity', 'Correlated Wiretap Channels', 'Eavesdropping Scenarios']

title: New Results in Secrecy Analysis of Mixed RF/FSO Cooperative Relaying Networks
authors: Tonk, VK; Dwivedi, VK; Upadhya, A; Singh, SP; Yadav, PK
Main Research Question: How does the presence of eavesdroppers and hardware impairments affect the secrecy performance of mixed RF/FSO cooperative relaying systems?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs a mixed RF/FSO cooperative relaying system model with the RF link characterized by Nakagami-m fading and the FSO link by Malaga distribution, considering atmospheric turbulence and pointing errors. The analysis includes the derivation of closed-form expressions for the average secrecy rate (ASR) using the extended generalized bivariate Fox H-function (EGBFHF). Asymptotic expressions for ASR are also derived for high SNR conditions on both RF and FSO links.
Results: The results indicate that the presence of an eavesdropper and hardware impairments significantly reduce the ASR of the mixed RF/FSO system. The study provides both exact and asymptotic expressions for ASR, demonstrating the impact of these factors under various conditions.
Discussion: The study highlights the vulnerability of mixed RF/FSO systems to eavesdropping and hardware impairments. It emphasizes the need for robust security measures in such systems, particularly in scenarios with high SNR where the impact of these factors is pronounced. The use of EGBFHF in deriving the ASR expressions provides a comprehensive analytical tool for evaluating system performance under these adverse conditions.
Conclusions: The research concludes that hardware impairments and eavesdropping significantly compromise the secrecy performance of mixed RF/FSO relaying systems. The study suggests that addressing these vulnerabilities is crucial for enhancing the security of such communication systems.
Future Work: Future research should explore more advanced mitigation techniques for hardware impairments and eavesdropping in mixed RF/FSO systems. Additionally, the study of other fading models and their impact on the secrecy performance could provide deeper insights into system vulnerabilities and improvements.
Proposed Keywords: ['Mixed RF/FSO Relaying', 'Secrecy Rate', 'Hardware Impairments', 'Atmospheric Turbulence', 'Eavesdropping Impact']

title: Channel prediction for intelligent FSO transmission system
authors: Song, S; Liu, YJ; Xu, TM; Liao, SS; Guo, L
Main Research Question: How can the predictability of FSO channel conditions be enhanced to improve transmission stability and adaptability under varying weather conditions?
Methods and Experiments: The study involved the establishment of a FSO transmission testbed and the use of an environmental chamber to simulate real-world weather conditions. RSSI data was collected from these setups. Expanded GRU neural networks were then employed for FSO channel prediction, utilizing a true meteorological dataset and the collected RSSI data. The study also involved extensive analysis of the autocorrelation in RSSI data to validate the predictability of the channel conditions.
Results: The results indicated that the proposed GRU-based prediction model could predict FSO channel fading with high precision. Specifically, the absolute percentage error (APE) was less than 6.9% for up to 90% of the predictions. The study also demonstrated the ability of the model to handle different transmission distances and various weather scenarios effectively.
Discussion: The study highlighted the effectiveness of using machine learning techniques, particularly GRU neural networks, for predicting FSO channel conditions. The ability to predict channel conditions with high accuracy is crucial for optimizing FSO communication systems, especially in environments affected by adverse weather. The research also discussed the implications of these findings for the design of more robust and adaptive FSO systems.
Conclusions: The research confirmed that employing GRU neural networks for the prediction of FSO channel conditions significantly enhances the adaptability and reliability of FSO communication systems under varying weather conditions. The proposed model not only predicts the channel conditions with high accuracy but also supports the development of intelligent FSO systems that can dynamically adjust to changing environmental conditions.
Future Work: Future research should explore the integration of other machine learning models to compare effectiveness and efficiency. Additionally, extending the experiments to outdoor settings and incorporating real-time data acquisition could further validate the robustness of the proposed model. There is also a potential to explore the application of these predictive models in other areas of optical communications.
Proposed Keywords: ['FSO Channel Prediction', 'GRU Neural Networks', 'Weather Impact on FSO', 'Adaptive FSO Systems', 'Machine Learning in Optical Communications']

title: Secure FSO communication based on optical frequency-hopping technology using delay interferometers
authors: Wang, J; Jin, Y; Xie, Z; Chen, YF; Liu, Y; Zhu, NH
Main Research Question: How can optical frequency-hopping (OFH) technology using delay interferometers enhance the security of Free-Space Optical (FSO) communications?
Methods and Experiments: The study introduces a novel OFH scheme utilizing optical delay interferometers for secure FSO communication. The method involves carrier suppression modulation using a Mach-Zehnder modulator, followed by series connection of a phase modulator and a delay interferometer to convert phase-modulated light into intensity-modulated light, producing OFSK signals. Simulations were conducted for a 5 km free-space link and back-to-back transmission at a rate of 10 Gbps to validate the scheme's feasibility. Security performance was also analyzed by calculating the eavesdropping probability.
Results: The simulation results confirmed the feasibility of the proposed OFH scheme, demonstrating successful transmission over a 5 km free-space link and in back-to-back setups at 10 Gbps. The security analysis indicated a robust security profile, with the probability of successful eavesdropping being significantly low, thereby establishing a secure space for the communication system.
Discussion: The study highlights the effectiveness of the proposed OFH scheme in enhancing the security of FSO communications through the innovative use of optical delay interferometers. The ability to convert phase-modulated signals to intensity-modulated ones using the DI and the control over sideband frequencies contribute to the robustness against eavesdropping. The research also discusses the compatibility of the OFH scheme with existing WDM systems and its potential integration with conventional encryption methods for enhanced security.
Conclusions: The proposed OFH scheme utilizing optical delay interferometers effectively enhances the security of FSO communications. The scheme's feasibility and robust security profile were demonstrated through simulation, showing potential for practical implementation in secure optical communications. Future work could explore integration with quantum cryptography and other advanced security technologies.
Future Work: Future research directions include exploring the integration of the OFH scheme with quantum cryptography to enhance security further. Additionally, investigating the impact of environmental factors such as temperature and humidity on the system's performance and developing methods to mitigate these effects are recommended. Further increasing the transmission rate through advanced modulation formats could also be pursued.
Proposed Keywords: ['Optical Frequency-Hopping', 'Delay Interferometers', 'Free-Space Optical Communications', 'Physical Layer Security', 'Optical Frequency-Shift Keying']

title: Physical layer security in MIMO hybrid FSO-mmWave systems: A learning-based link selection approach
authors: Tokgoz, SC; Althunibat, S; Miller, SL; Qaraqe, KA
Main Research Question: How can the secrecy performance of MIMO hybrid FSO-mmWave systems be maximized through learning-based link selection in the presence of various types of eavesdroppers?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs a deep learning approach, specifically convolutional neural networks (CNNs), to optimize link selection in hybrid FSO-mmWave systems. The CNN models are trained to select the optimal set of antennas and lasers for transmission based on the system's channel state information (CSI), which includes factors like channel estimation errors, weather conditions, pointing errors in FSO systems, link distances, signal-to-noise ratios, and path losses. The performance of the CNN-based link selection is compared against conventional methods and other machine learning algorithms such as support vector machines (SVM) and naive-Bayes (NB) under various system conditions and eavesdropper scenarios.
Results: The CNN-based link selection scheme demonstrated equivalent performance to the conventional link selection methods, with the added benefit of reduced computational complexity and faster processing times. The results also highlighted the robustness of the CNN approach under different physical layer conditions and eavesdropper scenarios, maintaining high secrecy performance across varying signal-to-noise ratios, channel estimation errors, and atmospheric conditions.
Discussion: The study underscores the effectiveness of using CNNs for link selection in complex MIMO hybrid FSO-mmWave systems, particularly in enhancing physical layer security against eavesdropping. The CNN models effectively handle the high dimensionality and non-linear relationships of the system's parameters. The comparison with traditional and other machine learning-based methods demonstrates the superiority of CNNs in terms of speed and performance consistency.
Conclusions: The proposed CNN-based link selection scheme provides a powerful tool for enhancing the secrecy performance of hybrid FSO-mmWave systems, offering a significant improvement over traditional methods in terms of computational efficiency and adaptability to various eavesdropping scenarios and physical conditions. This approach is particularly suitable for dynamic and complex backhaul networks in 5G and beyond technologies.
Future Work: Future research should explore the integration of more advanced machine learning techniques, such as reinforcement learning or federated learning, to further optimize link selection processes. Additionally, extending the study to include real-world testing and implementation in 5G networks could validate the practical applicability and efficiency of the proposed methods under actual operating conditions.
Proposed Keywords: ['Hybrid FSO-mmWave Systems', 'Physical Layer Security', 'Convolutional Neural Networks', 'Link Selection', 'MIMO Systems']

title: A PHY Layer Security Analysis of a Hybrid High Throughput Satellite With an Optical Feeder Link
authors: Illi, E; El Bouanani, F; Ayoub, F; Alouini, MS
Main Research Question: How can the physical layer security performance of a hybrid very high throughput satellite communication system with an FSO feeder link be enhanced?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs a combination of theoretical analysis and Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate the physical layer security. The satellite communication system uses selection combining technique to combine signals received through various optical apertures and employs zero-forcing precoding to mitigate interbeam interference. The security analysis considers the presence of eavesdroppers at both the satellite and ground station links. Statistical properties of the signal-to-noise ratios for both legitimate and wiretap links are derived to evaluate the intercept probability metric.
Results: The results indicate that the use of multiple optical apertures enhances the security up to a certain limit, beyond which additional apertures do not improve secrecy. Furthermore, zero-forcing precoding enhances system security compared to scenarios without precoding, particularly for specific positions of nodes relative to eavesdroppers.
Discussion: The study highlights the effectiveness of using multiple optical apertures and advanced signal processing techniques like zero-forcing precoding in enhancing the security of satellite communications against eavesdropping. The limitations in the number of apertures and the dependency on node positions for optimal security performance are discussed. Comparisons with existing satellite communication systems are made to underscore the improvements offered by the proposed system.
Conclusions: The research concludes that employing multiple optical apertures and zero-forcing precoding significantly enhances the physical layer security of hybrid satellite communication systems with FSO links. The study also identifies the optimal conditions under which these technologies are most effective, providing a pathway for future enhancements in satellite communication security.
Future Work: Future research should explore the integration of more advanced signal processing techniques and investigate the impact of dynamic environmental conditions on the security performance. Additionally, expanding the analysis to include quantum key distribution within the FSO links could offer further insights into achieving unbreakable security.
Proposed Keywords: ['Hybrid Terrestrial-Satellite Systems', 'Free-Space Optical Communications', 'Physical Layer Security', 'Zero-Forcing Precoding', 'Intercept Probability']

title: A Review on Deployment of UAV-FSO System for High-Speed Communication
authors: Tumma, Y; Kappala, VK
Main Research Question: What are the key challenges and potential solutions for deploying UAV-FSO systems for high-speed communication?
Methods and Experiments: The review synthesizes existing research on UAV-FSO systems, focusing on challenges such as atmospheric turbulence, pointing errors, and energy limitations of UAVs. It discusses various solutions like energy harvesting, advanced modulation techniques, and machine learning applications for optimizing system performance. The paper also examines the integration of UAVs with FSO technology through simulation studies using OptiSystem 7.0 to model different atmospheric conditions and their impact on communication links.
Results: The review identifies that atmospheric conditions like fog, rain, and turbulence significantly affect the FSO link performance. Solutions such as dual-hop relaying, modulating retroreflectors, and intelligent reflecting surfaces are proposed to mitigate these effects. Energy harvesting techniques are suggested to extend UAV operational time, and advanced modulation schemes are recommended for improving data transmission reliability under varying atmospheric conditions.
Discussion: The paper discusses the integration of UAVs with FSO technology as a promising approach to overcome bandwidth and security limitations of traditional RF systems. It highlights the necessity of addressing atmospheric challenges and UAV energy limitations through innovative solutions like machine learning for adaptive control and modulation, energy harvesting, and robust system design to enhance the reliability and flexibility of UAV-FSO systems.
Conclusions: UAV-FSO systems offer a viable solution for high-speed and secure communication, especially in remote areas. However, their effectiveness is contingent upon overcoming significant challenges related to atmospheric interference and UAV energy constraints. Future research should focus on refining energy harvesting techniques, exploring advanced modulation methods, and leveraging machine learning to optimize system performance under dynamic conditions.
Future Work: Future research should explore the integration of UAV-FSO systems with emerging technologies such as IoT and edge computing, develop lightweight and energy-efficient PAT systems suitable for compact UAVs, and apply machine learning algorithms for real-time adaptive control and anomaly detection to enhance system reliability and security.

title: Advanced Control Architectures for Quantum Satellite Temporal-Networking
authors: Chiti, F; Picchi, R; Pierucci, L
Main Research Question: How can the deployment of Satellite Quantum Networks (SQNs) using Software-Defined Networking (SDN) technology and Temporal Networks (TNs) optimization effectively manage the rapid variability of satellite topologies and enhance global quantum communication?
Methods and Experiments: The study introduces an SDN-based architecture for managing SQNs, utilizing Temporal Networks (TNs) theory for dynamic optimization of satellite paths. The architecture includes a Master Control Station (MCS) and an SDN Controller embedded in the satellite constellation. The proposed path selection algorithm operates on a temporal graph representing the satellite constellation, optimizing for the longest duration of contact between satellites and ground stations. The performance of the proposed framework was evaluated using simulations based on the Iridium NEXT constellation data, considering worst-case scenarios of ground station placements.
Results: The results demonstrate that the proposed SDN-based architecture and TNs optimization strategy can effectively manage the rapid changes in satellite topology and optimize the path durations. The simulations show that the average duration of optimal paths is about 276.9 seconds, and the system can maintain connectivity and support distributed applications by exploiting all available connection opportunities, even in worst-case scenarios.
Discussion: The study highlights the effectiveness of integrating SDN and TNs in managing SQNs, particularly in dynamic and rapidly changing environments like LEO satellite constellations. The proposed architecture allows for more efficient management of quantum communication links, potentially enhancing the performance of global quantum networks. The discussion also compares this approach with traditional satellite communication systems, emphasizing the advantages of quantum technologies in terms of security and computational capabilities.
Conclusions: The proposed SDN-based control architecture and TNs optimization for SQNs provide a viable solution for managing dynamic satellite topologies and enhancing global quantum communications. The framework supports high entanglement rates and robust connectivity, which are crucial for the deployment of global Quantum Internet and Quantum Cloud services.
Future Work: Future research will focus on further refining the SDN-based architecture and TNs optimization algorithms to handle larger satellite constellations and more complex scenarios. Additionally, exploring the integration of quantum cryptographic techniques such as Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) within SQNs could enhance security and privacy in quantum communications.

title: AirQKD: The Role of Free-Space Optics Quantum Key Distribution Enabling Pragmatic Secure and Scalable Communications
authors: Davidson, ZCM; Hugues-Salas, E; Bonner, GM; Jones, BE; Prentice, J; Kariappa, S; Fowler, DS; Oliveira, RD; Zhang, P; Andersson, Y; Kosmatos, EA; Stavdas, A; Lord, A
Main Research Question: How can Free-Space Optical (FSO) communications be effectively integrated with Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) to enhance secure communications in practical, real-world settings?
Methods and Experiments: The study involved the design and deployment of a Free-Space Optical (FSO) system integrated with Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) technology, specifically using the BB84 protocol. The system comprised a QKD transmitter ('Alice') and a QKD receiver ('Bob'), with subsystems for electronic/photonic and optical components. The hardware included single photon detectors, single photon sources, quantum random number generators, and sophisticated telescope systems with dynamic alignment capabilities. Experiments were conducted in real-world settings, testing the system over distances up to 300 meters, with considerations for atmospheric conditions and alignment challenges.
Results: The system achieved a link loss of 12.3 dB in initial tests, with subsequent integration of quantum hardware predicting a total loss of 15.2 dB for QKD, including detector losses. Background light levels were controlled to around 5000 Hz per QKD channel, suitable for daylight operation. The mean photon number was set to 0.7 for the signal state intensity of the decoy state protocol, and the security key rate (SKR) was estimated around 453.8 kb/s based on the GLLP privacy amplification equation for BB84, considering infinite key transmission.
Discussion: The integration of FSO with QKD presents a viable solution for enhancing secure communications, particularly in environments where traditional fiber optics are impractical. The study highlighted the importance of precise alignment and atmospheric considerations in deploying such systems. The results demonstrated the potential for FSO-QKD systems to operate effectively in real-world conditions, offering a scalable and secure communication method that complements existing technologies like 5G.
Conclusions: The AirQKD project successfully demonstrated the feasibility of integrating Free-Space Optical communications with Quantum Key Distribution for secure, scalable communications. The study provided valuable insights into the practical deployment of FSO-QKD systems, highlighting their potential to enhance network security and connectivity, particularly in last-mile applications. Future work will focus on optimizing system components and expanding the range and stability of the communication links.
Future Work: Future research will explore enhancements in hardware integration for reduced losses and improved alignment stability. Additionally, extending the communication range and developing robust protocols for varying atmospheric conditions will be crucial. Methods and Experiments: The study involves theoretical derivation of secrecy outage probability (SOP) and average secrecy capacity (ASC) for a mixed RF-FSO system with a wireless-powered jammer. The RF link experiences Nakagami-m fading while the FSO link undergoes Exponentiated Weibull fading. A two-hop decode-and-forward relay system is analyzed. Monte-Carlo simulations are used to verify the derived expressions. The impact of factors such as average interference noise ratio, number of jammer antennas, time block allocation factor, and size of the receiving aperture on the system's secrecy performance is evaluated through simulations.
Results: The results indicate that increasing the average interference noise ratio, the number of jammer antennas, the time block allocation factor, and the size of the receiving aperture significantly enhances the system's secrecy performance. Specifically, higher interference noise ratios and more jammer antennas reduce the secrecy outage probability (SOP) and increase the average secrecy capacity (ASC).
Discussion: The study highlights the effectiveness of incorporating a wireless-powered friendly jammer in enhancing the security of mixed RF-FSO systems. The use of a save-then-transmit protocol allows for controlled energy harvesting and interference transmission, which significantly improves the system's resistance to eavesdropping. The findings suggest that careful adjustment of system parameters such as jammer antenna count and aperture size can optimize secrecy performance.
Conclusions: The introduction of a wireless-powered friendly jammer with a save-then-transmit protocol significantly improves the physical layer security of mixed RF-FSO systems. The study provides valuable insights into the design and optimization of secure communication systems under various environmental and system-specific conditions.
Future Work: Future research should explore the integration of advanced modulation techniques and more complex jamming protocols to further enhance the security of mixed RF-FSO systems. Additionally, experimental validation of the theoretical models in real-world scenarios would be beneficial to confirm the practical applicability of the proposed solutions.

title: On Secure Free-Space Optical Communications Over Malaga Turbulence Channels
authors: Saber, MJ; Sadough, SMS
Main Research Question: How does the Málaga (M) turbulence model impact the performance of secure free-space optical communications, particularly in terms of secrecy capacity, secrecy outage probability, and strictly positive secrecy capacity?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs a theoretical analysis combined with Monte-Carlo simulations to evaluate the performance of secure FSO communications over Málaga turbulence channels. The analysis includes deriving closed-form expressions for key security metrics such as average secrecy capacity, secrecy outage probability, and strictly positive secrecy capacity, considering the effects of intensity modulation/direct detection (IM/DD) and pointing errors. The Málaga model is used to represent the atmospheric turbulence, which is a general model encompassing both log-normal and Generalized-K models.
Results: The derived expressions provide a unified framework for assessing security performance across different turbulence conditions. Simulation results confirm the analytical derivations, showing that the security performance improves with increasing average SNR of the main channel. Additionally, the results indicate that the secrecy outage probability improves with better pointing accuracy, and the strictly positive secrecy capacity increases with the decrease in turbulence intensity.
Discussion: The study highlights the effectiveness of the Málaga model in capturing the complex dynamics of FSO channels under security constraints. It is shown that the model can effectively be used to predict the performance of secure FSO links under various atmospheric conditions. The results also emphasize the importance of considering pointing errors in the design of secure FSO systems.
Conclusions: The research confirms that the Málaga turbulence model is a robust tool for analyzing the security performance of FSO communications. The study provides valuable insights into how different factors such as pointing errors and turbulence conditions affect the security of FSO links. The findings suggest that improving pointing accuracy and optimizing channel conditions can significantly enhance the security of FSO communications.
Future Work: Future research should explore the integration of advanced modulation techniques and adaptive optics to further enhance the security and reliability of FSO systems under more diverse atmospheric conditions. Additionally, experimental validation of the theoretical models under real-world conditions would be beneficial to confirm the practical applicability of the findings.

title: On Secure Mixed RF-FSO Decode-and-Forward Relaying Systems With Energy Harvesting
authors: Saber, MJ; Mazloum, J; Sazdar, AM; Keshavarz, A; Piran, MJ
Main Research Question: What is the impact of various channel conditions and energy harvesting on the security performance of mixed RF-FSO communication systems?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs a dual-hop RF and FSO transmission system with a source, a destination, an information receiver, and an energy receiver acting as an eavesdropper. The system uses decode-and-forward (DF) relaying and energy harvesting from the RF signal. The RF channels are modeled with Nakagami-m fading, and the FSO channel is modeled with Málaga turbulence and pointing errors. Analytical expressions for the average secrecy capacity (ASC) and secrecy outage probability (SOP) are derived using the probability density function (PDF) and cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the SNR for both RF and FSO channels.
Results: The results provide closed-form expressions for ASC and SOP, demonstrating how these metrics are influenced by system parameters such as the power splitting ratio, the turbulence conditions, and the pointing errors. The study confirms that the physical-layer security performance improves with increasing SNR at the relay and destination, and deteriorates with higher SNR at the eavesdropper.
Discussion: The discussion highlights the effectiveness of integrating RF and FSO technologies with energy harvesting to enhance security performance in wireless communication systems. It also emphasizes the importance of considering various channel impairments and system parameters in designing secure communication systems. Comparisons with existing models show that the proposed system can effectively mitigate eavesdropping risks under specified conditions.
Conclusions: The study concludes that the proposed mixed RF-FSO system with DF relaying and energy harvesting can significantly enhance the security performance by properly managing the power splitting for information decoding and energy harvesting. It also suggests that the system's resilience to eavesdropping can be optimized by adjusting system parameters according to the channel conditions.
Future Work: Future research should explore the integration of more advanced channel models and adaptive power splitting techniques to further enhance the security and efficiency of mixed RF-FSO systems. Additionally, experimental validation of the proposed models under real-world conditions would be beneficial to confirm the theoretical findings.

title: On Secure Mixed RF-FSO Systems With TAS and Imperfect CSI
authors: Lei, HJ; Luo, HL; Park, KH; Ansari, IS; Lei, WJ; Pan, GF; Alouini, MS
Main Research Question: How does the secrecy outage performance of mixed RF-FSO systems with transmit antenna selection (TAS) schemes and imperfect CSI affect the overall security of the communication system?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs a dual-hop relay system with MIMO RF links and an FSO link, considering outdated and imprecise CSI for RF and FSO links, respectively. Four TAS schemes are proposed to enhance secrecy performance. The analysis involves deriving closed-form expressions for PDF and CDF over Málaga channels with imperfect CSI, and for the equivalent SNR at the legitimate receiver over Nakagami-m and Málaga channels. Monte-Carlo simulations are used to validate the analytical results.
Results: The study finds that outdated CSI significantly impacts the secrecy performance of mixed RF-FSO systems. The results also show that increasing the number of antennas at the source does not significantly enhance secrecy performance. The derived expressions for PDF and CDF, as well as the bounds for EST, provide insights into the effects of misalignment and detection technology on system performance.
Discussion: The discussion highlights the challenges posed by outdated and imprecise CSI in mixed RF-FSO systems and the limited impact of increasing antenna numbers at the source on enhancing secrecy. The effectiveness of the proposed TAS schemes in mitigating these challenges is also discussed, with a focus on the role of system parameters such as misalignment and detection technology.
Conclusions: The study concludes that outdated CSI has a significant negative impact on the secrecy performance of mixed RF-FSO systems. While increasing the number of antennas at the source does not substantially improve secrecy performance, the proposed TAS schemes effectively enhance security under the conditions of imperfect CSI. The study underscores the importance of considering CSI imperfections in the design and analysis of secure mixed RF-FSO communication systems.
Future Work: Future research should explore the integration of advanced error-correcting codes and more sophisticated antenna selection algorithms to further enhance the secrecy performance of mixed RF-FSO systems. Additionally, investigating the impact of more complex channel conditions and incorporating machine learning techniques for predictive analysis and adaptive system optimization could provide further improvements in system security.

title: On the Performance of Mixed FSO/RF SWIPT Systems With Secrecy Analysis
authors: Singh, R; Rawat, M; Jaiswal, A
Main Research Question: How does the performance of a mixed FSO/RF SWIPT system with secrecy analysis behave under the influence of pointing errors, atmospheric turbulence, and energy harvesting, and what are the implications for physical layer security?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs a dual-hop mixed FSO/RF SWIPT system with decode-and-forward relaying. The FSO link is modeled with Málaga (M) distributed turbulence and pointing errors, while the RF link is subjected to double shadowed Rician fading. Statistical characteristics such as probability density function, amount of fading, average bit error rate, outage probability, and ergodic capacity are derived analytically. Physical layer security metrics including secure outage probability and strictly positive secrecy capacity are also derived considering scenarios with one or two eavesdroppers.
Results: The results demonstrate that pointing errors, atmospheric turbulence, and energy harvesting significantly affect the system performance metrics such as BER, OP, and ergodic capacity. The system's resilience to eavesdropping attacks varies based on the number of eavesdroppers and the type of link they access (FSO or RF).
Discussion: The study highlights the critical role of atmospheric conditions and system configurations in the performance and security of mixed FSO/RF SWIPT systems. It is shown that higher levels of turbulence and pointing errors degrade the system performance but can potentially enhance secrecy by reducing the eavesdropper's received signal quality. The integration of SWIPT with dual-hop FSO/RF systems poses unique challenges and opportunities for secure and efficient communication.
Conclusions: The mixed FSO/RF SWIPT system exhibits complex behavior under various atmospheric and system conditions. Effective management of pointing errors and turbulence is crucial for optimizing system performance and security. The study provides foundational analytical expressions that can aid in the design and analysis of secure FSO/RF communication systems.
Future Work: Future research should explore adaptive techniques for mitigating pointing errors and turbulence effects. Additionally, the integration of advanced coding schemes and more sophisticated energy harvesting models could further enhance the performance and security of mixed FSO/RF SWIPT systems.

title: On the Physical Layer Security of Mixed FSO-RF SWIPT System With Non-Ideal Power Amplifier
authors: Singh, R; Rawat, M; Jaiswal, A
Main Research Question: How can the physical layer security of a mixed FSO-RF SWIPT system be enhanced in the presence of non-ideal power amplifiers under various eavesdropping scenarios?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs a dual-hop mixed FSO-RF SWIPT system model with non-ideal power amplifiers. The FSO link is modeled under Málaga (M)-turbulence with pointing errors, while the RF link undergoes double shadowed Rician fading. The physical layer security is analyzed through closed-form expressions for secrecy metrics such as secure outage probability, strictly positive secrecy capacity, and secrecy throughput. Three eavesdropping scenarios are considered: FSO-side, RF-side, and simultaneous FSO- and RF-side attacks. Asymptotic approximations are derived to determine the secrecy diversity order, and the impacts of SWIPT parameters and PA efficiency on secrecy performance are explored.
Results: The results indicate that the security and reliability of the proposed system can be significantly enhanced by using efficient power amplifiers, particularly at the RF front end. The system's security can be manipulated based on the eavesdropper’s location and controlled through SWIPT parameters. The study also finds that the system is more susceptible to eavesdropping attacks as the double shadowing becomes more severe.
Discussion: The study highlights the critical role of power amplifier efficiency and SWIPT parameters in enhancing the physical layer security of mixed FSO-RF systems. It is demonstrated that efficient power amplifiers can significantly mitigate the risk of eavesdropping, especially in RF-dominated scenarios. The research also underscores the importance of considering different eavesdropping scenarios and their impact on system security. Comparisons with existing works reveal that the proposed system offers improved security metrics under realistic PA models and complex fading conditions.
Conclusions: The proposed mixed FSO-RF SWIPT system with non-ideal power amplifiers offers a robust framework for enhancing physical layer security against various eavesdropping scenarios. Efficient utilization of power amplifiers and careful adjustment of SWIPT parameters can significantly improve both the security and reliability of the system. Future research should focus on optimizing these parameters under dynamic environmental conditions and exploring the integration of advanced cryptographic techniques.
Future Work: Future research should explore the integration of adaptive beamforming techniques and advanced cryptographic measures to further enhance the physical layer security of mixed FSO-RF systems. Additionally, the impact of dynamic environmental conditions on system performance and security should be investigated, along with the development of more sophisticated models for non-ideal power amplifiers.

title: On the Physical Layer Security of a Decode and Forward Based Mixed FSO/RF Co-Operative System
authors: Pattanayak, DR; Dwivedi, VK; Karwal, V; Ansari, IS; Lei, HJ; Alouini, MS

The secrecy performance metrics such as secrecy outage probability are derived using Meijer’s G-function and bivariate Fox’s H-function. Results: The study provides exact closed-form expressions for secrecy outage probability, which are validated through Monte-Carlo simulations. The results indicate that the system's secrecy performance can be significantly affected by the type of eavesdropper and the specific characteristics of the FSO and RF links. Discussion: The analysis highlights the critical role of the distribution models in assessing the PHY security of mixed FSO/RF systems. The study discusses the implications of different eavesdropping scenarios and the effectiveness of the DF relay strategy in enhancing security. Comparisons with existing models demonstrate the robustness of the proposed approach under various conditions of turbulence and fading.
Conclusions: The research concludes that physical layer security in mixed FSO/RF systems can be effectively enhanced by accurately modeling the signal fading and employing advanced mathematical functions for performance analysis. The study underscores the importance of considering multiple eavesdropping scenarios and using hybrid distribution models to accurately assess and improve the security of such systems.

title: On the Secrecy Capacity of Hybrid FSO-mmWave Wiretap Channels
authors: Tokgoz, SC; Althunibat, S; Miller, SL; Qaraqe, KA
Main Research Question: How can the secrecy performance of hybrid FSO-mmWave communication systems be quantitatively analyzed and enhanced in the presence of various types of eavesdroppers under different atmospheric and fading conditions?
Methods and Experiments: The study employs a theoretical analysis combined with Monte-Carlo simulations to evaluate the secrecy performance of hybrid FSO-mmWave systems. The communication system is modeled to operate under exponential atmospheric turbulence for FSO links and Weibull fading for mmWave links. Different types of eavesdroppers (RF-, FSO-, and Hybrid-Eve) are considered to assess the system's vulnerability. The secrecy capacity is analyzed by deriving exact analytical expressions for the probability of strictly positive secrecy capacity (SPSC) under varying channel conditions and eavesdropper capabilities.
Results: The results demonstrate that the secrecy performance of the hybrid FSO-mmWave system is significantly influenced by the type of eavesdropper and the channel conditions. The analytical expressions for the probability of SPSC were validated against Monte-Carlo simulations, showing exact agreement. The study highlights that Hybrid-Eve, capable of eavesdropping on both FSO and mmWave links, poses the greatest threat to the secrecy performance of the system.
Discussion: The study discusses the implications of different eavesdropping scenarios on the secrecy performance of hybrid FSO-mmWave systems. It is noted that the integration of FSO and mmWave technologies offers robustness against specific channel impairments but also introduces new challenges in maintaining secure communications. The effectiveness of the proposed analytical framework in predicting system performance under various eavesdropping scenarios is also highlighted.
Conclusions: The research concludes that hybrid FSO-mmWave systems must carefully consider the impact of different types of eavesdroppers and channel conditions on their secrecy performance. The study emphasizes the need for developing advanced security measures that address the unique challenges posed by the hybrid nature of these systems. Future work should focus on enhancing the security protocols and exploring adaptive measures to mitigate the risks posed by sophisticated eavesdroppers.
Future Work: Future research should explore the development of adaptive security mechanisms that can dynamically adjust based on the detected eavesdropper type and channel conditions. Additionally, investigating the integration of quantum key distribution with hybrid FSO-mmWave systems could offer a promising avenue for enhancing physical-layer security.

title: On the Secrecy Enhancement of an Integrated Ground-Aerial Network With a Hybrid FSO/THz Feeder Link
authors: Illi, E; Qaraqe, M
Main Research Question: How can the security of HAP-aided ground–aerial communication networks be enhanced to mitigate the risks posed by aerial and ground eavesdroppers using a hybrid FSO/THz transmission scheme?
Methods and Experiments: The study introduces a hybrid FSO/THz transmission scheme leveraging multiple HAPs to enhance secrecy in ground–aerial communications. The network model includes a ground station communicating with a legitimate user via HAPs, with potential eavesdropping by both aerial and ground adversaries. The proposed scheme's performance is analyzed by deriving an analytical expression for the secrecy outage probability (SOP), considering the impact of atmospheric conditions, pointing errors, and the diversity provided by multiple HAPs.
Results: The results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid FSO/THz scheme significantly enhances network security. Specifically, the SOP is reduced by four orders of magnitude when using four HAPs compared to a single-HAP system. Additionally, a 5-dB secrecy gain is achieved over the benchmark THz-only feeder link system.
Discussion: The study highlights the effectiveness of integrating multiple HAPs with a hybrid FSO/THz transmission to improve the secrecy of ground–aerial communications. The diversity of HAPs and the robustness of hybrid transmission under various atmospheric impairments contribute to substantial security enhancements against potential eavesdroppers. The results are compared with existing single-HAP and THz-only systems, demonstrating superior performance of the proposed scheme.
Conclusions: The proposed hybrid FSO/THz transmission scheme effectively enhances the secrecy of HAP-aided ground–aerial networks. By leveraging multiple HAPs, the scheme offers significant improvements in resilience against eavesdropping, making it a viable solution for secure high-data-rate communications in challenging vertical propagation environments.
Future Work: Future research should explore the integration of advanced adaptive algorithms for real-time optimization of HAP selection and link management based on dynamic environmental conditions and security requirements. Additionally, the potential integration of quantum key distribution in the hybrid FSO/THz scheme could be investigated to further enhance the security of the communication system.

title: Opportunistic Schedule Selection for Multiuser MIMO FSO Communications: A Security- Reliability Trade-Off Perspective
authors: Shakir, WMR; Charafeddine, J; Al Satai, H; Hamdan, H; Haddad, S; Sayah, J

The system model includes a transmitter with multiple users and a single receiver with multiple apertures, operating over generalized Malaga-M turbulence channels. The TAS combined SNR distributions are derived, and Monte Carlo simulations are conducted to validate the numerical results. The analysis includes the derivation of closed-form expressions for outage probability, average bit error rate, intercept probability, and SRT.
Results: The results demonstrate that TAS significantly enhances the security, reliability, and SRT performance of MU-MIMO FSO systems. The study also highlights the diversity advantages provided by channel variations due to atmospheric turbulence and generalized nonzero boresight pointing errors.
Discussion: The study discusses the effectiveness of TAS in improving the performance metrics of MU-MIMO FSO systems under varying atmospheric conditions. It compares the TAS approach with traditional methods, emphasizing its potential to address existing challenges in FSO communications. The integration of TAS with MU-MIMO configurations is shown to effectively mitigate risks associated with eavesdropping and signal degradation due to turbulence.
Conclusions: The research concludes that opportunistic transmit aperture selection (TAS) is a viable strategy to enhance the security and reliability of MU-MIMO FSO systems, particularly in environments characterized by generalized Malaga-M turbulence. The approach not only improves performance metrics such as outage probability and bit error rate but also effectively manages the security-reliability trade-off.
Future Work: Future research should explore the scalability of TAS in larger MU-MIMO FSO systems and its integration with advanced cryptographic techniques. Additionally, experimental validation in real-world atmospheric conditions would further substantiate the theoretical findings.

title: Optical Wireless Communications: Research Challenges for MAC Layer

Addressing these challenges is crucial for the successful implementation of OWC technologies in green wireless communication systems. The paper calls for more focused research on developing application-specific MAC layers that can effectively handle the identified challenges.

This includes innovative approaches to managing hidden nodes, optimizing GTS allocation, enhancing mobility support in OWPANs, and improving fast link recovery mechanisms. title: Performance Enhancement of FSO Communication System Under Rainy Weather Environment Using a Novel Encryption Technique
authors: El-Mottaleb, SAA; Mohamed, AG; Ahmed, HY; Zeghid, M
Main Research Question: How can the performance of Free-Space Optical (FSO) communication systems be enhanced under adverse rainy weather conditions using a novel encryption technique?
Methods and Experiments: The study introduces a novel image encryption technique utilizing the Choquet Fuzzy Integral (CFI) combined with integer wavelet transform to enhance the security and performance of FSO communications under rainy conditions. Experiments were conducted using authentic meteorological data from Alexandria, Egypt, and Jeddah, KSA, to simulate real-world environmental impacts on FSO systems. Performance metrics such as FSO range, SNR, PSNR, and SSIM were evaluated to assess the effectiveness of the proposed encryption method.
Results: The results indicate that the novel encryption technique significantly enhances the resilience of FSO communications against environmental disturbances caused by rain. The maximum FSO range for transmitting high-quality encrypted images was found to be 1055 m under heavy rain conditions, which could be extended up to 2290 m under light rain conditions. Additionally, the city of Jeddah, with its lower average rainfall intensity, demonstrated a further extension of the encrypted image's travel range by an additional 2400 m compared to Alexandria.
Discussion: The study highlights the effectiveness of integrating the Choquet Fuzzy Integral with integer wavelet transform for encrypting images transmitted via FSO channels. This approach not only secures the data but also mitigates the adverse effects of rainy weather on signal quality and transmission range. The use of real-world meteorological data adds practical relevance to the findings, suggesting that the proposed method could be effectively applied in diverse geographical and environmental conditions.
Conclusions: The novel encryption technique based on the Choquet Fuzzy Integral and integer wavelet transform significantly improves the performance and security of FSO communication systems under rainy conditions. The method proves particularly effective in extending the propagation range of encrypted images, thereby enhancing the reliability and applicability of FSO technology in adverse weather conditions.
Future Work: Future research should explore the adaptation of the proposed encryption technique to other environmental challenges such as fog, dust, and haze. Additionally, further studies could investigate the integration of this encryption method with other advanced optical technologies to enhance the overall performance and security of FSO systems.

title: Performance Evaluation and Security Analysis of UAV-Based FSO/CV-QKD System Employing DP-QPSK/CD

The integration of CV-QKD with UAV-based FSO systems was shown to enhance security against eavesdropping. The research also underscored the importance of optimizing system parameters to achieve desired performance metrics and demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed optimizations in mitigating the impacts of channel impairments and UAV positional deviations.
Conclusions: The research concluded that UAV-based FSO systems employing CV-QKD can achieve robust performance and security by optimizing key system parameters. The study provided valuable insights into the design and operation of secure UAV-based FSO communication systems under practical conditions, including turbulence and potential eavesdropping threats.

title: Performance Evaluation of Dual Hop Mixed FSO RF System Using Differential Chaos Shift Keying With Secrecy Analysis
authors: Narang, G; Aggarwal, M; Kaushal, H; Kumar, A; Ahuja, S; Shukla, NK
Main Research Question: How can the performance and secrecy of dual-hop mixed FSO RF systems employing differential chaos shift keying (DCSK) be optimized under various atmospheric conditions and fading models?
Methods and Experiments: The study investigates three dual-hop communication systems: FSO-FSO, RF-FSO, and FSO-RF, all using decode-and-forward relaying. Differential chaos shift keying (DCSK) is employed to enhance system confidentiality. The RF link is modeled with Nakagami-m fading, while the FSO link is affected by Gamma-Gamma turbulence and pointing errors. The performance metrics analyzed include average bit error rate (BER) and secrecy outage probability (SOP).

Conclusions: The study concludes that physical-layer security in FSO communications is highly susceptible to eavesdropping, particularly when the eavesdropper is near the transmitter. Discussion: The study highlights the complex impact of channel correlation on the secrecy performance of FSO communications. Contrary to the typical expectation that increased correlation always degrades performance, the findings demonstrate that under certain conditions, increased correlation can actually enhance secrecy performance. This counterintuitive result suggests that the correlation can be exploited strategically to improve the security of FSO systems under specific atmospheric conditions.
Conclusions: The research concludes that the secrecy outage performance of FSO communications is significantly influenced by the correlation between the main and wiretap links. The study establishes that while increased correlation generally leads to a degradation in secrecy performance, there exists a critical threshold beyond which further increases in correlation can enhance secrecy performance. This insight is crucial for designing more secure FSO systems in environments with correlated fading channels.

Future work should explore the integration of less sensitive SDR hardware to extend the effective range and capacity of secured FSO links.

Conclusions: The research concludes that the use of multiple relays and paths significantly enhances the effective secrecy throughput of relay-assisted FSO communications, especially under challenging weather conditions and eavesdropping scenarios. title: Utilizing polarization-multiplexing for free space optical communication transmission with security operation

Methods and Experiments: The study utilized a 10 Gbit/s OOK FSO system with polarization-multiplexing. A 1.5μm laser diode was used at the central office, connected to a polarization controller and a Mach-Zehnder Modulator for generating FSO modulation data. The system transmitted through a 25 km single-mode fiber and a 1000 m free space link. Polarization-multiplexing was achieved using two polarizers with orthogonal directions, creating FSOp and FSOs signals as data and interference channels respectively. The FSOp and FSOs signals acted effectively as data and interference channels, with the interference mechanism proving crucial for security by deteriorating the BER when the FSOs power exceeded −30 dBm. The results also demonstrated the system's capability to handle significant fiber and free space transmission lengths while maintaining security.
Conclusions: The polarization-multiplexing technique significantly enhances the security of FSO communication systems by using orthogonal polarization signals to create interference. The system supports long-distance transmission both through fiber and free space, proving its effectiveness and robustness in secure optical communications.

title: A Survey on Physical Layer Security for FSO Communication Systems

It examines various physical layer security techniques, including noise randomization, channel state information (CSI) utilization, and the use of multiantenna and cooperative nodes. The paper also discusses the application of secrecy capacity measures and the impact of atmospheric conditions on security.
Results: The review identifies that while FSO offers enhanced security over RF due to its narrow beam and line-of-sight operation, it is vulnerable to eavesdropping, especially when the eavesdropper is located near the transmission path or the receiver. Techniques such as using acousto-optic deflectors and employing advanced modulation schemes like orbital angular momentum multiplexing are highlighted as effective in improving secrecy performance under various atmospheric turbulence conditions.
Discussion: The paper discusses the advantages of physical layer security techniques over traditional cryptographic methods, particularly in terms of computational efficiency and the ability to secure data without the need for shared keys. It also highlights the ongoing need for research into robust security solutions that can operate effectively across the diverse conditions encountered in FSO communications.
Conclusions: FSO systems present a viable alternative to RF systems for high data rate transmissions, offering inherent security advantages due to their physical properties. However, the technology faces significant security challenges, particularly from sophisticated eavesdropping techniques. Continued research and development of physical layer security strategies are critical to fully leverage the potential of FSO systems in future wireless communications.
Future Work: Future research should focus on developing new physical layer security techniques that are specifically tailored to the unique characteristics of FSO systems. title: Information Security Risks Outside the Laser Beam in Terrestrial Free-Space Optical Communication
authors: Zou, DF; Xu, ZY
Main Research Question: What are the information security risks associated with terrestrial FSO communication systems when an eavesdropper is located outside the laser beam, and how do these risks vary with atmospheric conditions and eavesdropper's location?
Methods and Experiments: The study utilizes the Kim model to calculate atmospheric attenuation coefficients for various wavelengths and visibility conditions. Link gains for both line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) channels are derived, incorporating factors like divergence attenuation and atmosphere attenuation. Theoretical analysis, Monte Carlo ray tracing simulation, and experimental evaluations are used to determine NLOS channel gains. The secrecy capacity is calculated using Wyner's secrecy capacity concept, and the secrecy capacity outage probability is analyzed under different turbulence conditions using statistical models.
Results: The results indicate that information security risks are negligible under high-visibility conditions but become significant under low-visibility conditions. The study also maps the secrecy capacity for different eavesdropper locations, showing a 2D distribution of insecure regions. Additionally, the secrecy capacity outage probability is highly sensitive to atmospheric turbulence, background radiation, and the required transmission rate.
Discussion: The findings highlight the complexity of securing FSO communications against eavesdropping, particularly under adverse atmospheric conditions. The study emphasizes the importance of considering both LOS and NLOS channels in security analyses and suggests that the system's vulnerability to eavesdropping increases with decreasing visibility and stronger atmospheric turbulence.
Conclusions: The research concludes that terrestrial FSO communication systems face significant security risks from NLOS eavesdropping, especially under low visibility and strong turbulence conditions. Effective security measures must account for both LOS and NLOS vulnerabilities and adapt to varying atmospheric conditions to ensure secure communication.
Future Work: Future research should focus on enhancing the models for predicting NLOS link gains and developing more robust methods for securing FSO communications under diverse atmospheric disturbances. Further experimental studies are also recommended to validate the theoretical models and simulations used in this study.

title: Securing and auto-synchronizing communication over free-space optics using quantum key distribution and chaotic systems

A Lorenz chaotic system is used for data transmission over a classical channel, while QKD secures the exchange of chaotic system parameters over a quantum channel. Experiments involved simulating this setup to transmit images as binary data across an FSO channel, using techniques like Low-density-parity-check (LDPC) and Quadrature-Phase-Shift-Keying (QPSK) for noise minimization and error correction.

The system maintained a low bit-error-rate (BER) across varying signal-to-noise ratios (SNR), and the image data was accurately reconstructed at the receiver end without any pixel errors, even at very low SNR values.
Discussion: The study highlights the effectiveness of combining chaotic systems with QKD for securing FSO communications. The inherent unpredictability and broadband noise-like signals of chaotic systems, along with the unconditional security of QKD, significantly enhance the security against eavesdropping and other security threats. The results also suggest robustness against noise and potential applicability in long-range space missions.
Conclusions: The proposed communication protocol effectively enhances the security and synchronization of FSO communications through the integration of chaotic communications and QKD. The protocol not only improves security over traditional methods like N-slit interferometers but also extends the operational range, making it suitable for space missions. The experimental results confirm the protocol's feasibility and effectiveness.
